title: The AI Sell-Off Compared to Well-Known Stock Market Crashes: S&P 500 vs 1987, 2008 and Covid | Company Tracker
excerpt: The S&P 500 fell 4.4% on 5 Nov 2026, its worst day since April 2025, and is 6% below its 6 Oct record. Charted day by day against 1987, 2008, Covid and other falls since 1950.
content_text: 6 Nov 2026The recent AI sell-off brought a lot of fearmongering headlines. Put next to past stock market crashes, it's only a mild correction for the S&P 500, 6% below its record. Tech fell harder, with the Nasdaq down 11% and chip stocks down 36%, as much as they fell during Covid (35%). Its depth is the lowest close before the next record."AI sell-off" is our name for the slide since the 6 October 2026 record.The S&P 500 is not the same index it was in 1929 or 1973: technology is now about a third of it, far more than then, so a tech-led sell-off moves it more than it would have."Still below 2000 high" means the Nasdaq and chip stocks had not got back to their 2000 records by 2008, so 2008 is part of their dot-com fall, not a fall of its own.How we collect and check the data behind Company Tracker: About.More insights
